articles.headline: James, Embiid play 76ers' preseason finale, but 'still working on our rhythm'
articles.description: Without VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday night's 125-120 loss to the Celtics, 76ers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what this team may look like this season, including LeBron James and Joel Embiid playing preseason highs in minutes.
articles.headlineJa: ジェームズとエムビードがセブンティシクサーズのプレシーズン最終戦に出場、「まだリズムを整えている最中」
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜夜のセルティックス戦（125-120で敗戦）を欠場したVJエッジコム不在の中、レブロン・ジェームズとジョエル・エムビードがプレシーズン最多の出場時間を記録するなど、ニック・ナース監督率いるセブンティシクサーズは今シーズンのチームの姿を垣間見せる展開となった。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- As the Philadelphia 76ers begin a season with a star-laden roster, center Joel Embiid rejects the narrative that anyone needs to sacrifice for this team to succeed.

"I'm against the concept of sacrificing," he said after Friday's preseason finale. "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat."

Albeit without second-year starting guard VJ Edgecombe, who was held out of Friday's 125-120 loss to the Boston Celtics for precautionary reasons, Sixers coach Nick Nurse gave the closest glimpse of what this Sixers team may look like this season.

The other active Sixers starters -- LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Embiid -- all played preseason highs in minutes and well into the second half. Embiid, who struggled in his last appearance two games ago against the Brooklyn Nets, finishing with six points and eight turnovers, was dominant.​

He scored 27 points, grabbed eight rebounds and added five assists. In the third quarter, he had one of the game's best highlights when he threw down an emphatic dunk that drew roars from fans at Xfinity Mobile Arena. "It's good to dunk. I thought I would never dunk again," Embiid said with a smile. "I guess I don't know what happened. I kind of got possessed."

Still, the group never looked comfortable together on the floor, despite playing against Celtics reserves. After the game, players didn't shy away from their somewhat disjointed performance. Brown pointed to the team's spacing Friday night, which he said led to turnovers, as one of the many things they need to fix moving forward.

"We're not where we want to be yet," he said. "So that's just a part of it. It's a part of coming together, a new group with a bunch of guys, different style, but we just got to keep getting better every day."

James echoed Brown's comments, but neither seemed concerned about the Sixers' ability to eventually jell.

"We're getting there," James said. "I mean, obviously we are a couple of weeks in, so we're still working on our rhythm, working on our kinks, and it's not going to be perfect."

The Sixers open the regular season against the New York Knicks on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Titans CEO apologizes to fans, supports Robert Saleh, GM
articles.description: Titans CEO Burke Nihill said the organization believes that coach Robert Saleh and GM Mike Borgonzi are "ultimately going to get this team out of the woods."
articles.headlineJa: タイタンズCEOがファンに謝罪、ロバート・サレ監督とGMへの支持を表明
articles.descriptionJa: タイタンズのバーク・ニヒルCEOは、ロバート・サレ監督とマイク・ボルゴンジGMが「最終的にチームを苦境から救い出す」と組織として信じていると述べた。
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Titans CEO Burke Nihill, who is empowered to speak on behalf of controlling owner Amy Adams-Strunk, said the organization fully believes in coach Robert Saleh and general manager Mike Borgonzi and will have patience with them.

The Titans are 0-5 in Saleh's first season as coach and have won only three games since Borgonzi joined the team prior to the 2025 season. Overall, the franchise has won just six games dating to the 2023 season.

"I personally feel a sense of stability," Nihill told ESPN on Friday. "I believe that Mike Borgonzi and Robert Saleh are ultimately going to get this team out of the woods and restore it to competitive football. The train is on the tracks. It just hasn't picked up momentum, but it will.

"I can confidently say this organization is in a place where there is organizational belief in Mike, in Robert, and they absolutely have all the support they need to get this train moving and moving faster."

Saleh's first season in Tennessee has not gotten off to a good start. The defense has generated only two turnovers, and the offense is averaging a league-low 246.4 yards and 11.6 points.

Regardless, Saleh said the Titans are sticking to their process, which he described as "rigorous and detailed," and vowed to put their best foot forward on Sundays.

"We're going through a lot of adversity," Saleh said. "But if we capture it the right way, we're going to find a lot of growth, and when I tell you guys that the sun is going to shine on this organization eventually, it's going to shine."

The Titans have fired a coach or general manager every year since 2022. They recently fired senior vice president of brand marketing Erin Swartz, senior vice president and chief revenue officer Adam Nuse and vice president of creative Charles Jensen.

When asked about the instability, Nihill said it's possible to be "agile while still being stable as a business."

Tennessee has lost 33 of its past 39 games and is stuck in a seven-game losing streak dating to Week 17 of last season. There was a lot of optimism that the Titans would take a big step toward respectability heading into the opening of Nissan Stadium next season, but a poor product has left many fans wondering when they will get another win.

"The first thing I would say back to the fans is just that we're sorry," Nihill told ESPN. "There's nobody in this building that doesn't feel ... a sense of grief about it, because not only are we fans of the team as well, but we feel the sense of responsibility to deliver. And we've let our fans down because football is supposed to be fun.

"I think it starts on the field and the state of the franchise. We're 0-5, and that's not nearly good enough. It hasn't been for a while."

Liverpool are in pole position to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, while Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae is on the radar of Arsenal. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

- Liverpool are in pole position to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, according to the Daily Mail. The 23-year-old, whose transfer is valued at £100 million, has drawn widespread interest from major clubs including Chelsea, though he is currently sidelined after sustaining an injury on his full England debut. But Liverpool are confident that having former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola in charge will help their case.

- Arsenal are interested in signing Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae during the January transfer window, reports Bild's Christian Falk. The Gunners are seeking defensive cover following an injury to Piero Hincapié, though the 29-year-old South Korea international could also be offered a contract extension to remain in Bavaria.

- Should a January deal for Scott fall through, Liverpool have compiled scouting dossiers on AS Monaco's Lamine Camara and Roma's Manu Koné, TEAMtalk reports. However, the Reds face competition for €55 million-rated Camara -- with Chelsea maintaining interest alongside Aston Villa, Newcastle United, Crystal Palace and Brighton & Hove Albion -- while Koné has been linked with Real Madrid, Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United.

- USMNT prospect Mathis Albert is considering leaving Borussia Dortmund to secure regular first-team minutes, according to Sky Sports Deutschland. The 17-year-old winger has only made one appearance in the German Cup this season. He previously attracted interest from Paris Saint-Germain in 2025, while Manchester City and Chelsea were also looking at signing him for around €20 million.

- Tottenham Hotspur will demand a £75 million fee to consider letting right back Pedro Porro move to Barcelona or Real Madrid, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old signed a five-year contract extension in the summer, significantly strengthening Spurs' position as they aim to retain him past 2027.

Other rumors

- Ex-Liverpool star Steven Gerrard could take over at Wrexham, as current boss Phil Parkinson is under increasing pressure at the Championship club. (TalkSPORT)

articles.headline: Xabi Alonso not ready to say if Chelsea heading 'right way'
articles.description: Xabi Alonso said it is too early to tell whether Chelsea are going the "right way" as he looks for greater balance from his free-scoring team.
articles.headlineJa: シャビ・アロンソ、チェルシーが「正しい方向」に向かっているかは判断せず
articles.descriptionJa: シャビ・アロンソは、得点力の高い自身のチームにさらなるバランスを求めており、チェルシーが「正しい方向」に向かっているかを判断するにはまだ早すぎると述べた。
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso said it is too early to tell whether Chelsea are going the "right way" as he looks for greater balance from his free-scoring team.

A chaotic start to life under the Spanish coach sees the Blues sit as the third-highest scorers in the Premier League with 15 goals from their six games, yet no team in the division has conceded more than their 13.

- Alonso: Reece James may be out beyond Christmas

- Ranked: Who are the best 50 players in the Premier League so far this season?

- Moisés Caicedo determined to repay Alonso's faith

In total there have been 28 goals scored in Chelsea's league games so far with six more coming in last weekend's 5-1 win over Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

"You need a lot of clean sheets to win trophies," Alonso said. "But you need to score a lot of goals. So it's about being strong in defence, being good in attack and we are in that process.

"We are still early days. This first part we've been doing good things, other things to be improved. To do a very deep analysis, it's too early probably.

"In February we will have enough game to see where we are going and if it's the right way. But we are demanding in terms of what we are doing and what we can do better."

Much of the issue in conceding goals has come from a lack of control in midfield, a problem that appeared largely to have been fixed on Saturday as Moisés Caicedo made his first start of the season.

The return of the Ecuador midfielder after a calf injury brought far greater stability in the middle of the pitch, with Jordan Henderson, who scored his first two goals for the club as the Cherries were routed, also influential alongside him.

The pair are likely to be used together more than had been planned in the coming weeks with Reece James likely to be out until the new year after undergoing what the club called "minor" surgery on a knee problem.

"It's one game, but we saw positives," Alonso said. "Moises helps Hendo, Hendo helps Moises. I think as well Rom [Roméo] Lavia is in a good moment. He played 25 minutes and he did really well. We need not just two midfielders, we need more than that.

"In terms of personalities, they match well. Hendo he has this energy, he is very active, he covers a lot of pitch. He finds a balance with Moisés who is more in position, he has this stability to be in good distances with everything.

"It was a good start and we need to keep building from that."

Chelsea travel to face Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday knowing that a win will take them above David Moyes' side, with both teams currently on 10 points from six matches.

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta told Arsenal job cuts will help club 'achieve success'
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has been told Arsenal's redundancies will help the club "achieve the success we want to create" after it emerged the Premier League champions are set to cut 60 jobs.
articles.headlineJa: ミケル・アルテタ、アーセナルの人員削減がクラブの「成功達成」を助けると指摘される
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグ王者が60人の人員削減を行うことが明らかになったことを受け、ミケル・アルテタに対し、アーセナルの人員整理は「私たちが創り出したい成功」を達成する助けになるとの指摘がなされた。
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has been told Arsenal's redundancies will help the club "achieve the success we want to create" after it emerged the Premier League champions are set to cut 60 jobs.

Chief executive Richard Garlick informed staff this week that Arsenal's workforce will be reduced across a number of departments -- although the playing and coaching staff in the men's and women's teams will be unaffected.

- Arteta defends Gyökeres after goalless start to season

- Merino lucky 'to be alive' after Dortmund bus attack

- Forest sweating on Gibbs-White fitness vs. Arsenal

The cuts are set to impact up to 7% of the club's 871 permanent staff.

Arteta was last week rewarded with a new four-year deal, worth as much as £20 million ($27m) a season, after he oversaw Arsenal's first Premier League title since 2004.

Arsenal's turnover for the 2024-25 season was a record £691m ($920m).

"First, this question is not for me," Arteta said on Friday when asked about the expected job losses in his news conference ahead of Sunday's league match against Nottingham Forest.

"It was explained to me about the exercise, and the analysis that has been done across the club, and with the intention always to evolve to improve.

"Some decisions have to be taken to put people in the right roles, and keep investing, to achieve what we want to achieve the success that we want to create. That has been explained.

"Obviously, I am not the right person to answer to that question. That's for sure. And hopefully everybody will respect that."

Arteta did not take any further questions on the topic at the request of the club.

The 44-year-old Spaniard also confirmed that the club will retake Arsenal's official squad photo following William Saliba's omission.

The France international, who last season played an integral role in the club winning the league title, was conspicuous by his absence from the picture which was released on Thursday.

He is currently sidelined with a back problem, and Arsenal said he was not available because of a "medical appointment."

"We have tried to do that picture three times already," explained Arteta on Friday. "We had to cancel it at the last minute for different reasons.

"We have some commercial obligations, and we had people that flew over because of that. We decided to do that picture at least.

"We'll have another picture with the whole family. Hopefully we can get them all together at some point. He [Saliba] knows how loved he is. He's completely fine about it."

Saliba has not played since the World Cup but there is an outside chance he could be available before the international break next month.

Martín Zubimendi is in contention to face Forest despite sustaining an ankle injury in training directly after Arsenal's win over Leeds at the Emirates Stadium last weekend. Piero Hincapié, who also suffered an ankle problem during the post-match session, will not feature.
